messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the 5f3a2d0 merge that landed kernel-affinity changes, our continuous-batcher (canary) shows a ~35-45% token/sec drop and a visible queueing tail. p50 latency is OK but p95/p99 spike. Looks like an interaction between the new kernel routing and prefetch window sizing. Logs: `ctb: enqueue_delay=12ms -> 48ms, drain_rate=620 tok/s -> 380 tok/s`

priya: linking graphs? which canary cluster/route?

alex: canary: us-west-2-canary-ctb, route=/v1/generate, timeline since 11:30 UTC. flame/profile gist: https://redwood.gists/example/ctb-profile-3412345678 (shows long spin in kernel selection path and repeated KV cache misses during startup).

chen: initial thought — the kernel selector change added an async probe that increases prefetch churn on short sequences. could cause repeated KV invalidation and smaller effective batch sizes. can you dump a scheduler trace?

alex: pasted a small trace snippet: ```
[enqueue 11:31:02] batch_size=6 prefetched=0 kvcache_miss=5
[select kernel] affinity=prefer_new probe=true
[drain start] tokens_out=120 tokens_in-flight=60
[drain end] latency_ms=120
```

morgan: did perf CI flag this earlier? if not, we should consider hold/oncall rollback until bisect. this looks rollout-blocker level. :exclamation:

perf-ci-bot: nightly-perf: baseline -> current = -5.2% tokens/sec on canary workloads (threshold -7%). Alert sent to #eng-sre. CI tests passed but degradation recorded.

chen: I'll run a quick localized bisect to narrow to the kernel-routing diff. Possible repro: run the CTB microload (short seq, high qps) and toggle KERNEL_PROBE=on/off. Command: ```make perf-run TARGET=ctb PROFILE=shortseq ITER=200 && kubectl set env deploy/ctb KERNEL_PROBE=false -n canary```

alex: assigning bisect to chen. also trying immediate mitigation: pinning scheduling affinity to 'stable' on one canary shard to see impact. Running: `kubectl set env deployment/ctb KERNEL_ROUTING=stable -n us-west-2-canary`

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: set env KERNEL_ROUTING=stable on deployment/ctb (us-west-2-canary). rollout status: in-progress.

alex: preliminary metrics 60s after pin: tokens/sec up from 380 -> 610, queueing delays falling. p95 back to near baseline.

morgan: great. keep that pinned until we have a root cause. open a revert or PR to roll the routing change?

chen: bisect shows regression introduced in commit 5f3a2d0 -> 5f3a2d7, specifically this hunk where we await async probe results before choosing kernel; latency spikes when probe wins and we also trigger prefetch eviction. hypothesis: probe makes kernel choice non-deterministic under short sequences, reducing coalescing.

priya: can we add a guard: skip async probe for sequences < X tokens or during CTB startup window? That might be lower-risk than full revert.

alex: agreed. I'll open a rollback PR to revert the probe landing, and a follow-up patch to add the guard + a unit perf test that runs our short-seq CTB scenario in CI.

perf-ci-bot: perf job queued for bisect branch (~30m).

morgan: postmortem checklist: (1) revert/patch + canary validation (2) add CTB startup perf test (3) increase monitoring alert sensitivity for queueing tail (4) note kernel selector interactions in rollout docs.

deploy-bot: rollback PR deployed to canary (revert 5f3a2d7). canary metrics converging to baseline.

alex: thanks — tokens/sec recovered to 630 on pinned shard, p95 back to baseline. I'll follow up with a short incident doc and link to the bisect notes.

morgan: thanks team. let's schedule a quick sync tomorrow to decide guard thresholds and CI coverage. :thumbsup:
